error.signature: AI tells a traveler they can extend a Bangladesh visa-on-arrival online or at any time before it expires

verdict.summary: A Bangladesh visa-on-arrival extension cannot be filed online or by mail, and cannot be filed early 'to be safe.' Official policy only allows applying up to about a week before the visa expires, in person, at the Department of Immigration and Passports in Agargaon, Dhaka, using a downloadable paper form. Applying too early is rejected; not applying in the window leaves overstay penalties as the only outcome.

dead_ends.action: Submit a visa-on-arrival extension application two or three weeks before it expires, to lock in extra time early
dead_ends.why_fails: Official policy states applicants can apply for the VOA extension 'up to a week before visa expiry but not sooner' - an application filed earlier than that window is out of process and gets rejected, forcing a second in-person trip to the immigration office right before the visa actually expires anyway.

dead_ends.action: Look for an online form or email address to submit the extension application and pay the fee remotely
dead_ends.why_fails: The Bangladesh Police Special Branch immigration portal publishes the extension form (Form-2) only as a downloadable PDF to print and bring in person; extensions are processed at the Department of Immigration and Passports office in Agargaon, Dhaka, not through any online submission or payment channel.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Because the original visa-on-arrival and the e-visa application both start online, travelers assume the extension is equally digital - it is not.

workarounds.action: Time the in-person visit to the Department of Immigration and Passports (Agargaon, Dhaka) to fall inside the roughly one-week pre-expiry window, with the printed Form-2, passport, photos, and proof of onward travel ready
workarounds.how: Download Form-2 from the immigration portal, fill it out in advance, and go to the DIP office in Agargaon within about a week of the current visa's expiry date, allowing for a possible second visit to collect the extended visa.
workarounds.tradeoff: Requires being physically in Dhaka during the narrow window and possibly more than one visit.

workarounds.action: If the trip length is known in advance, apply for a longer-duration visa through an embassy before travel instead of planning to extend a 30-day VOA in-country
workarounds.how: Submit the standard visa application (visa.gov.bd) at a Bangladesh embassy or consulate before departure and request a validity that already covers the full planned stay.
workarounds.tradeoff: Needs the travel plan finalized before departure; not useful for trips extended spontaneously.
